target_customer: Individuals and small businesses wanting a simple website or online store
problem: Building a website required HTML and design skills; non-technical people wanted a WYSIWYG drag-and-drop builder.
business_model: freemium SaaS subscriptions plus payments and add-ons

founders.name: David Rusenko
founders.background_notes: Built the first product in a dorm room as a student

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser WYSIWYG editor with hosting and templates was standard web engineering with some hard front end parts in 2006.

defensibility.rationale: Many similar builders appeared; scale, templates and hosted customers gave limited lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors grew alongside it; Square bought Weebly in 2018 for about $365M.

market_need_then: Penn State required students to keep online portfolios, giving an early use case; VentureBeat noted demand for WYSIWYG site building around 2007.

branding.name_origin: Not explained in sources; one naming blog says it came from a search for an available domain, unconfirmed.
branding.domain_note: weebly.com, reportedly picked for being available (unconfirmed single source)

identity.voice_and_tone: encouraging and supportive, 'It's your business. You've got this.'

brand_strength.rationale: Weebly was widely recognized as an easy website builder with 20M+ users per YC page, but little brand-specific evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Weebly grew from a Penn State dorm project into a freemium site builder with over 20 million users, raised from Sequoia and Tencent, and was valued at about $455M in 2014 per press. Competition from Wix and Squarespace limited growth and Square bought it for about $365M in April 2018, below the earlier valuation.
notes: Funding sources conflict: Series B 2011 from Sequoia (undisclosed), $15M 2012 from Tiger and Insight and $30M 2013 Sequoia in one source; Dealroom 2014 $35M valued at $140M vs $455M in Onward State; Crunchbase total of $35.7M. Only the 2014 Series C is recorded, valuation left null. 2015 valuation of $490M by Business Insider via Crunchbase, unverified. weebly.com footer copyright 2019 shows Square ownership. Founders' education from the Penn State student sources. Founded 2006, YC Winter 2007. Competitor Wix launched 2006, others like GeoCities and Google Page Creator not confirmed. No sourced logo or name origin.
